subject: Social Studies
stem: Following the district reorganisation in Andhra Pradesh (2022), the number of districts in the state increased from 13 to:
explanation: In April 2022, Andhra Pradesh reorganised its 13 erstwhile districts into 26 new districts to improve administrative efficiency. (Telangana separately went from 10 to 33 districts in its own 2016 reorganisation — a commonly confused figure.)

section: Social Studies · Ch49 — Andhra Pradesh: History & Geography
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Pattiseema Lift Irrigation Scheme was built to transfer surplus water from the Godavari river to which other river basin in Andhra Pradesh?
explanation: Pattiseema lifts Godavari flood waters into the Polavaram Right Main Canal, linking it to the Krishna basin — supplementing irrigation and drinking water supply for the Krishna delta.

stem: The Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi, whose kingdom lay in the Godavari-Krishna delta region, are historically significant for patronising early:

options.option_text: Telugu literature (including the beginnings of Telugu Mahabharata translation under Nannaya, patronised by Rajaraja Narendra)
Introduction of the printing press to India
First contact between India and Europe
Establishment of the Mughal administrative system

explanation: Eastern Chalukya king Rajaraja Narendra of Vengi patronised Nannaya, who began the Telugu Andhra Mahabharatam — a foundational moment in Telugu literary history, unrelated to printing, European contact, or Mughal administration.

section: Social Studies · Ch49 — Andhra Pradesh: History & Geography
subject: Social Studies
stem: Andhra Pradesh is often called the 'Rice Bowl of India' primarily because of extensive paddy cultivation in the fertile delta regions of the:
explanation: The Krishna and Godavari deltas, with their fertile alluvial soil and extensive canal irrigation, produce vast quantities of rice — earning coastal Andhra this title. Ganga-Yamuna and Narmada-Tapi are outside AP entirely.
